# `vos_document`: the marker skeleton of a generated implementation document

`vos_document.tokens` and `vos_document.grammar` read the **skeleton** of
`code/specs/<impl>.warrant`, the document `vos-link gen-doc` assembles
([VOS02](../../specs/VOS02-interface-contracts-and-profile-linking.md) section 2.3,
decision D-GD5): which lines are marker comments and in what order they come.  Every
other line is a plain `LINE`, handed to `warrant-grammar` unread.

```text
warrant vos_ready_bitmap v1
  -- vos02:generated by vos-link gen-doc; do not edit; contract-package=vos_ready_contract
  -- vos02:contract-begin sha256=<64 hex>
  ...
  -- vos02:contract-end
  -- vos02:impl-begin
  ...
  -- vos02:impl-end
  -- vos02:obligations-begin tier=<safety|representation|policy|canonical|any> sha256=<64 hex>
  ...
  -- vos02:obligations-end
  assume platform:
    none
  assume environment:
    none
```

## How a forged marker is refused

* The token grammar has **seven exact line tokens**, one per marker, and a catch-all
  `FORGED` token for *any* other line that contains `-- vos02:`: a wrong indent, extra
  text, an unknown marker name, a marker in a string literal or after code.  The engine
  tries definitions in file order and takes the first that matches, so a line that is not
  exactly a marker falls through to `FORGED`.
* The parser grammar has no rule that mentions `FORGED`, so it is a token with no place.
  (`validate` therefore prints one intended warning: `FORGED` is defined but never used.)
* The parser grammar spells the order: header, generated, contract block, implementation
  block, obligations blocks, trailer.  Each marker occurs exactly once because the rule
  has room for exactly one.
* A `.part` is lexed with the *same* token grammar and admitted only if it lexes to plain
  lines, so the writer and the reader can never disagree about what a marker looks like.

The one `skip` entry matches nothing (`[^\s\S]`).  The engine refuses an empty skip group,
and with none at all it skips leading blanks, which would hide an indented forged marker
and change the bytes a digest is taken over.

Consumed by [`rust/vos-manifest`](../../packages/rust/vos-manifest); validated by its
`tests/grammars.rs`.
